title: Daily vs. Monthly SIP: Building Wealth with Mutual Funds
description: A ₹100 daily SIP invests approximately ₹3,000-₹3,100 per month, similar to a ₹3,000 monthly SIP, but with different timing. Daily SIPs offer finer rupee cost .

faq.q: Is a daily SIP always better than a monthly SIP?
faq.a: Not necessarily. While a daily SIP offers finer rupee cost averaging, the difference in final corpus, especially over shorter periods, might be marginal. The "better" option depends on your cash flow, convenience, and the availability of the option.

faq.q: Do all mutual funds offer daily SIPs?
faq.a: No, not all mutual fund houses or schemes offer daily SIPs. It's important to check with your specific fund house or investment platform to see if this option is available for the funds you wish to invest in.

Rupee cost averaging is an investment strategy where you invest a fixed amount regularly, regardless of market conditions. This helps average out the purchase cost of units over time, reducing the risk of investing a lump sum at a market peak.

faq.q: Can I switch from a monthly SIP to a daily SIP?
faq.a: Yes, generally you can modify your SIP instructions. You would typically need to stop your existing monthly SIP and then set up a new daily SIP with the desired amount and frequency through your fund house or investment platform.

faq.q: Are there any extra charges for daily SIPs?
faq.a: Generally, there are no additional charges specifically for choosing a daily SIP frequency over a monthly one. The expense ratio of the fund remains the same regardless of your SIP frequency.

faq.q: What if I miss a daily SIP payment?
faq.a: If your bank account has insufficient funds on a daily SIP debit date, the transaction for that day might fail. Most systems will simply skip that day's investment, and the SIP will resume on the next scheduled day. Repeated failures could lead to the SIP being cancelled by the fund house.

However, some of the specific corpus projections, while illustrative, might be slightly optimistic compared to other sources, and the claim about transaction charges is outdated.
